purpose: Measure ASM-1 (each academic source is fast, complete and permissive enough to serve a 3 s discovery search) and ASM-2 (the share of discovered papers with a retrievable open-access PDF) before any M4 production code exists, and record frozen candidate pools for phases 2, 7 and 8.
hashing: protocol_sha256 is the SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes of json.dumps(protocol, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False). Canonical JSON rather than raw bytes, because core.autocrlf=true rewrites line endings on checkout, so a raw-byte hash taken on Windows would not reproduce on a Linux checkout. Every results file records it.

rules.pre_registration: Everything in this file is fixed before the first live call. A departure from it is recorded as a deviation in every results file, never made silently.
rules.no_repeats: No request is ever repeated. A failure is an outcome: classified, recorded and counted. The one exception is deviation DEV-1. If a run stops part-way, it resumes by sending only planned requests the log does not already contain.
rules.secrets: Keys are read from spike/.env (OPENALEX_API_KEY, required; S2_API_KEY, optional), sent only in request headers to their own API host, and never written to a URL, a log line or a results file.
rules.s2_data_stays_local: Nothing Semantic Scholar returns (titles, abstracts, identifiers, links) is written to a tracked file. S2 appears in tracked files only as counts, timings and statuses; S2 identifiers and S2-only URLs are replaced by their SHA-256.
rules.pdfs_stay_local: Downloaded PDF bytes are written only under var/spike/pdf/ (gitignored) and are never committed.
rules.go_ahead: No live call is made before the owner's go-ahead on this protocol.

query_construction.normalise: Unicode NFKC, casefold, collapse whitespace runs to one space, strip. Applied to every phrasing before any source-specific step; mirrors the cache-key normalisation proposed for production. Casefolding also stops a capitalised word being read as an OpenAlex boolean operator.
query_construction.openalex: search = the normalised text with every '?' and '*' replaced by a space and whitespace re-collapsed (DEV-2). OpenAlex reads both as wildcards and refuses them in its default, stemmed search.
query_construction.semantic_scholar: query = the normalised text with every '-' replaced by a space and whitespace re-collapsed. S2's API reference: hyphenated query terms yield no matches.
query_construction.arxiv: terms = the normalised text split on every character that is not a letter or digit; drop arxiv_stopwords and tokens shorter than 2 characters; de-duplicate keeping first occurrence. search_query = 'all:<t1> AND all:<t2> AND ...'.

openalex.auth: Authorization: Bearer <OPENALEX_API_KEY>. Required: nothing runs without it, because the keyless allowance is for testing only.

params.filter: doi:<the 20 anchors' arXiv DataCite DOIs, https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.<id>, joined with |>

anchor_check.note: One list request. A miss means 'not found under its arXiv DOI', never 'absent from OpenAlex'.

single_record.ids: sampled with the seed from session-1 keyword results

semantic_scholar.auth: None by default: the shared unauthenticated pool. If S2_API_KEY is set it is sent as x-api-key, and every result records which mode ran.

search.note: The relevance-ranked endpoint. S2 recommends /paper/search/bulk for most uses, but bulk is not relevance-ranked, and relevance ranking is what discovery needs.

single_record.ids: sampled with the seed from session-1 keyword results

anchor_check.note: Also verifies every anchor's arXiv id: an id whose returned title does not normalise to the anchor's title is disabled for matching, and reported.

single_record.ids: sampled with the seed from session-1 keyword results

passes.what: Offline checks before any call. The address classifier runs against http_safety.self_test and must classify every entry correctly. The log checker runs against a synthetic log with one planted violation per rule and must flag each. A mutated copy of the checker, with its arXiv spacing rule removed, must fail that same test, which shows the check is load-bearing.

Session 1 search: 20 queries (10 topics x keyword and natural_language), in an order shuffled with the seed. A query's three requests start together, once every source's pacing gap has elapsed, with launch order shuffled with the seed.
Straight after P1: one anchor check per source, then single-record latency (OpenAlex 10, S2 10, arXiv 4).

Session 2: the 10 reversed_keyword queries with P1's concurrency and pacing, starting at least 6 hours after P1's last request. Same terms as session 1 in a different order, so no upstream cache can answer them and time of day is what varies.
Analysis and the log check. Writes spike/results/19_discovery_analysis.json and the findings.

budget.counting: Every HTTP request counts, including each redirect hop, which counts against the host it is sent to. A download is one work; its requests, hops included, count against download_requests_total_max and obey the same pacing.
budget.enforcement: The runner refuses any request that would exceed a maximum and records it as 'not sent (budget)'.

export.arxiv.org.why: arXiv API terms: no more than one request every three seconds, one connection at a time.

pacing.retry_after: A Retry-After from any host delays that host's next request by at least the stated time. The throttled request itself is not repeated.
pacing.host_stop: After 5 consecutive 429 or 5xx responses from one host, nothing more is sent to it this session; its remaining planned requests are recorded as 'not sent (host stopped)'.

timeouts_s.why_api_total_is_20: The slow tail must be observed, not cut off. A response slower than 20 s is recorded as a timeout at 20 s.

http_safety.schemes: https only. An http URL is never requested; its https form (same host, path and query) is tried instead, and the upgrade is recorded.
http_safety.ports: 443 only. A URL naming any other port is refused.
http_safety.addresses: The host is resolved before connecting. If any resolved address is not globally routable (Python ipaddress is_global false: loopback, private, link-local including 169.254.169.254, shared 100.64.0.0/10, documentation and benchmarking ranges, multicast, reserved, unspecified), the request is refused and recorded. IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses are unwrapped and judged as IPv4.
http_safety.known_gap: Resolving and then connecting leaves a DNS-rebinding window. The spike accepts it; the production guard (phase 5, D115) must connect to the address it checked.
http_safety.redirects: Never followed automatically. Each Location is a new hop, checked exactly like a first request. At most 5 hops; a hop that fails a check ends the chain as 'refused'.

byte_caps.note: Counted on decoded bytes. PDF hosts are sent Accept-Encoding: identity. 52428800 is MAX_PDF_BYTES (NFR-P8).

http_safety.credentials: API keys are sent only to their own API host. PDF hosts receive only the headers above. No cookies are kept.

pdf_probe.works: From session-1 keyword results: each source's ranks 1-10 per topic, merged into unique works (definitions.unique_work).
url_order: https://arxiv.org/pdf/<arXiv id>, if the work has one
pdf_probe.stop_rule: Probing a work stops at the first URL whose first bytes are %PDF- ('fetched'). A work with no candidate URL is 'no OA link'.
pdf_probe.recorded_per_attempt: Which sources supplied the URL; scheme; host; every hop (status, host, scheme, refusal reason); final status; Content-Type; Content-Length; whether the first bytes are %PDF-; duration; the licence each source reports for that location. URLs that only S2 supplied are recorded as host plus the SHA-256 of the URL.
pdf_probe.budget_exhausted: URLs left unprobed because a cap was reached are recorded as 'not probed (budget)', never dropped.

download_sample.select: Up to 30 'fetched' works chosen with the seed: up to 15 whose fetched URL is on arxiv.org, the rest from other hosts (all of them if there are fewer).
download_sample.checks: A full GET under http_safety, then scholiast.domain.upload.validate_upload (50 MiB cap and %PDF- magic) and scholiast.infrastructure.parsing.preflight.preflight (encrypted, no pages, no text layer): the production functions, unmodified. Recorded: bytes, then page count or failure class.

ASM-1a.question: Is each source fast enough for a 3 s search?
ASM-1a.measure: Session-1 search latency per source (request start to last body byte) over its 2xx responses, the connection-cold first request included: p50, p90, p95, max, n. Warm-only percentiles, and session 2's, are reported beside, never pooled. Completion curve over all 20 requests: share finished with a 2xx body within 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5 and 3.0 s, where a failure or timeout never completes; per source, and for all three sources together.
ASM-1a.pass_bar: p95 <= 2.0 s: fits. 2.0 < p95 <= 2.5 s: tight. p95 > 2.5 s: usable only truncated. Met if fits or tight.

ASM-1b.question: Is the metadata complete enough for FR-D1?
ASM-1b.measure: Share of session-1 records per source carrying: title, authors (at least 1), year, venue, abstract, citation_count, doi, arxiv_id, oa_link, full_date.
ASM-1b.pass_bar: title, authors and year >= 95%; abstract >= 70%; citation_count >= 95% for OpenAlex and S2. arXiv carries no citation counts by design, recorded as a structural gap rather than a failure.

ASM-1c.question: Are the free limits workable?
ASM-1c.measure: Per source: status counts, 429 count, Retry-After values, OpenAlex X-RateLimit-* headers (cost per request type), response bytes (p50, p95, max).
ASM-1c.pass_bar: OpenAlex (keyed): zero 429s. S2 keyless: 429s on <= 10% of its requests ('usable keyless'); S2 keyed: zero 429s. arXiv: zero 429s or 503s at the terms' pace.

ASM-1d.question: Is the relevance plausible?
ASM-1d.measure: Share of the 20 anchors in each source's top 10 and top 50, per phrasing, session 1. The P2 anchor checks separate 'not ranked' from 'not found in the source'.
ASM-1d.pass_bar: >= 50% of anchors in the top 50 for the keyword phrasing. A sanity bar, not a ranking evaluation.

ASM-2.question: How often can we fetch the PDF?
ASM-2.measure: Funnel over P3's unique works. L0: has at least one OA link. L1: at least one link usable over https, as given or upgraded. L2: fetched (first bytes %PDF- within 5 hops under http_safety). L3, on the P4 sample: within 50 MiB and passes validate_upload and preflight. Reported under allowlists A1 (arxiv.org only), A2 (the smallest set of final hosts covering >= 90% of L2 works, chosen greedily by count, ties alphabetical) and A3 (any host that passes http_safety).
ASM-2.denominator: Works whose probing finished. Works a cap left unprobed are reported separately and counted as neither success nor failure.
ASM-2.pass_bar: L2 under A3 >= 60% of unique works (doc 3's ASM-2 threshold). A1 and A2 are reported beside as evidence for the allowlist decision.

verdicts.ASM-1: PASS if at least two sources, one of them OpenAlex or S2, meet ASM-1a, 1b, 1c and 1d. PARTIAL if exactly one source meets all four. FAIL otherwise.
verdicts.ASM-2: PASS if L2 under A3 >= 60% of unique works; FAIL otherwise.

evidence_without_a_bar.allowlist: Initial and final host counts; http vs https as given; hop-count distribution; Content-Type; Content-Length; refusal reasons.
evidence_without_a_bar.dedup: Per source, the share carrying a DOI and an arXiv id; cross-source records linked by a shared identifier; title-only pairs (identical normalised titles of 3 or more tokens in different unique works); within-source same-title pairs; year spread among linked records (0, 1, 2 or more).
evidence_without_a_bar.licence: For each fetched work, the licence OpenAlex reports for the succeeding location (else best_oa_location) and any licence S2 reports; the share with none reported.
evidence_without_a_bar.stability: Per source, overlap of the top 10 between session-1 keyword and session-2 reversed_keyword results.
evidence_without_a_bar.phrasing: Keyword vs natural_language: result counts (zero-result rate, especially arXiv) and anchor recall.

definitions.normalised_title: NFKC, casefold, every character that is not a letter or digit becomes a space, collapse whitespace, strip.
definitions.doi: Lowercase; strip https://doi.org/, http://doi.org/ and doi: prefixes.
definitions.arxiv_id: Strip arXiv:, https://arxiv.org/abs/, http://arxiv.org/abs/ and https://arxiv.org/pdf/ prefixes, a trailing .pdf and a version suffix v<n>. The DataCite DOI 10.48550/arxiv.<id> maps to <id>.
definitions.arxiv_id_from_records: S2: externalIds.ArXiv. OpenAlex: a doi of the 10.48550/arxiv form, or any location whose landing_page_url or pdf_url is on arxiv.org. arXiv: the entry id.
definitions.anchor_match: A record matches an anchor if (a) its arXiv id equals the anchor's and that id passed the P2 arXiv check, or (b) its normalised title equals the anchor's. Near misses (token Jaccard >= 0.8 with an anchor title) are listed but not counted. The rule that matched is recorded for every hit.
definitions.unique_work: Union-find over records sharing a normalised DOI or arXiv id.
definitions.latency: time.perf_counter() from immediately before the request is issued to the last body byte read.

statistics.percentiles: Nearest rank, with n printed beside every percentile. No interval: at n=20, p95 is the 19th-ranked value and an interval on it says little.

deviations_pre_registered.DEV-1: If the first OpenAlex search returns HTTP 400 and its body names select or relevance_score, that one request is repeated once with relevance_score removed from select, every later OpenAlex request uses the reduced list, and the deviation is recorded in every results file. This is the only repeat the protocol allows.

DEV-2.found: Session 1, after 15 requests: all five OpenAlex searches sent (all natural_language, by the seeded order) returned HTTP 400, 'Wildcards (* or ?) require exact (no-stem) search', with X-RateLimit-Cost-USD 0. Every natural_language phrasing ends in '?'; no keyword or reversed_keyword phrasing contains '?' or '*'.
DEV-2.change: query_construction.openalex: '?' and '*' become spaces. Applies to every OpenAlex search sent after the amendment.
DEV-2.repeats: Each P1 OpenAlex search refused with HTTP 400 for a wildcard before the amendment is repeated once, after P1's last query and before P2, under request id <rid>/DEV-2, with the amended query. The repeat stands in for the refused request in the analysis, as DEV-1's would; the refusals stay in the log and are reported. The repeats run alone, not started together with the other two sources, and are marked. No other request is repeated.
DEV-2.dev1: DEV-1 applies to the first OpenAlex search that is not refused for a wildcard, since the first search was refused before its select list was judged.
DEV-2.budget: OpenAlex searches: 30 planned plus at most 5 repeats, within the maximum of 40.
DEV-2.s2: Not a deviation, recorded here for one place: S2 keyless returned 429 on its first five requests, the pacing.host_stop trigger, and stays stopped for session 1 as pre-registered.

DEV-A4-1.found: A4, 2026-10-09: the harness stopped part-way. 19 queries had run cold and repeated (starts s1 to s3 and the first of s4). The 20th cold search, t08-keyword in s4, began at 19:37:53 local; both sources answered (OpenAlex 1.33 s, arXiv 1.29 s); the machine had entered modern standby at 19:37:51 (Kernel-Power 506) and woke at 19:41:29 (507), and the client's 120 s timeout ended the harness. No Code Integrity block was logged. A stderr pipe the harness never read was tested offline as the cause and refuted (129 bytes per process). The harness kept client records in memory only, so part 1's result lists were lost; status, latency, per-source status and each search's window were rebuilt from its printed lines and the app's own log.
DEV-A4-1.verdict_already: Recorded before anything else runs: criterion 1 cannot be met by this run. Three of the 30 cold searches returned 503 (no source answered), so the nearest-rank p95 over 30 or 29 is a failed search, and OpenAlex was ok on 11 of 19 cold searches, so it cannot reach 24 whatever the rest do. The remainder runs for what A4 still owes: criterion 5's kills and the UI check, the first-after-start sample, the anchors and the cached latency.
DEV-A4-1.change: t08-keyword's cold search is void: excluded from every A4 number, its two source requests counted against the budget, and it is not repeated. The remaining queries of s4 (t01-natural_language, t07-reversed_keyword, t01-keyword, t04-keyword) run in a new start, s4b, whose first search is a first-after-start sample; then s5 and the kills as planned. The bars are computed over the 29 valid cold searches: nearest-rank p95 over 29, and each source ok on at least ceil(0.8 x 29) = 24. Part 1's searches have no result lists, so the anchors are reported for the topics whose keyword search ran in the remainder, with the others marked lost. The harness now writes each search's record to disk as it completes, and resumes from its logs.
DEV-A4-1.budget: Max raised to 55 OpenAlex searches and 50 arXiv queries (A4's budget.max is changed in place and refers here). Part 1 sent 28 and 24: OpenAlex failed on 8 of 19 cold searches, and each such repeat asked it again (D127), more than planned. The remainder needs about 10 cold searches to each, repeats of whatever fails, 3 kill searches asking each surviving source, 3 local attempts counted per killed source, and at most 3 UI searches.
DEV-A4-1.machine: The owner keeps the laptop's lid open and on power for the remainder; the app's keep-awake hold prevents idle sleep only.

A1.question: Does joining the query words with OR instead of AND put more anchors in arXiv's top 50?
A1.why: arXiv missed ASM-1d (35% of anchors in its top 50 for the keyword phrasing), and at least 7 of its 13 misses lack a query word in any form, so the AND construction excluded them before arXiv ranked anything (SPIKE-FINDINGS-M4.md 1d).
A1.queries: The 20 P1 queries: 10 topics x keyword and natural_language. Terms are built exactly as query_construction.arxiv; search_query joins them with ' AND ' (the same-day control) or ' OR ' (the treatment). Every other parameter as sources.arxiv.search.params. 40 requests.
A1.order: Seeded with stream '<seed>/A1': the 20 queries are shuffled, and within each query the order of AND and OR is shuffled.
A1.pacing: pacing['export.arxiv.org']: 3 s from the previous response end, one connection. Retry-After and the host-stop rule apply as in pacing.
A1.no_repeats: As rules: a failure is an outcome, and no A1 request is repeated.
A1.measure: Per construction and phrasing: anchors in the top 10 and top 50 (definitions.anchor_match, using the ids P2 verified), results returned, the reported total, and the zero-result rate. Latency per construction is reported, comparable because both run in the same window, and is not a decision input.
A1.decision_rule: Adopt OR iff, for the keyword phrasing, OR's top-50 anchor recall is >= 50% and strictly greater than the same-day AND's. Otherwise AND stays. If OR beats AND but is below 50%, AND stays and the gap is reported to the owner.
A1.outputs: Responses to data/eval/discovery-pools-arxiv-a1.json.gz with a manifest (arXiv metadata, CC0); numbers under addendum_a1 in spike/results/19_discovery_analysis.json; a section in SPIKE-FINDINGS-M4.md. The spike's committed pools are not changed.
does_not_establish: Anchor recall counts 20 famous papers and is blind to precision; OR may return more off-topic papers, which only phase 8's judged set can measure.
ASM-1 is not recomputed: a construction chosen after the fact cannot pass a bar retroactively.
One alternative is tested, so the anchors choose between two constructions, not among many.

A2.question: Which OpenAlex page size finishes within D122's 2.0 s source deadline, and what does a smaller page cost in anchors?
A2.why: OpenAlex missed ASM-1a (p95 2.61 s at 50 results) and finished within 2.0 s on 18 of the spike's 30 searches. Offline, from the frozen pools: authorships is 52% of a page and select takes only whole top-level fields; dropping locations would lose the arXiv id on 183 of 1,000 records; every response was already gzip and parsing takes under 10 ms. Page size is the lever left (D125). Numbered as the second addendum; unrelated to ASM-2's allowlist A2.
A2.queries: The 20 P1 queries: 10 topics x keyword and natural_language, each at per_page 50, 25 and 15. Every request, URL and headers, is built by the production adapter, scholiast.infrastructure.discovery.openalex.OpenAlexSource.request(text, limit=per_page): the spike's select list, with '?' and '*' replaced by spaces (D117). 60 requests.
A2.order: Seeded with stream '<seed>/A2': the 20 queries are shuffled, and within each query the order of the three sizes is shuffled. A query's three requests run back to back.
A2.connection: A new HTTP client, and so a new connection, for every request, as the production adapter opens one per search. Bodies are decoded as the client receives them, as in P1.
A2.pacing: pacing['api.openalex.org']: 1 s from the previous request start, one request at a time. Retry-After and the host-stop rule apply as in pacing.
A2.timeouts: timeouts_s.api_connect and api_total, as P1: the tail is observed, not cut at 2.0 s.
A2.no_repeats: As rules: a failure is an outcome, and no A2 request is repeated.
A2.measure: Per size, over all 20 requests: latency from request issued to last body byte, nearest-rank p50, p90 and p95 and the max, a failed request counted as slower than any success; the share finished within 2.0 s (Wilson); time to headers; body bytes; and the keyword-phrasing anchor recall within the page (definitions.anchor_match, using the ids P2 verified). Per query: whether the 25- and 15-result pages are, id for id and in order, the first 25 and 15 of the 50-result page. Cost from x-ratelimit-cost-usd.
A2.decision_rule: Ship the largest per_page in {50, 25, 15} whose p95 latency is <= 2.0 s AND whose keyword-phrasing anchor recall within its own page is >= 50%. If no size passes both, none is chosen and the owner decides.
A2.outputs: Responses to data/eval/discovery-pools-openalex-a2.json.gz with a manifest (OpenAlex data, CC0); numbers under addendum_a2 in spike/results/19_discovery_analysis.json; a section in SPIKE-FINDINGS-M4.md. The spike's committed pools are not changed.
does_not_establish: 20 requests a size make p95 the 19th-ranked value; a size that passes narrowly may not pass on another day.
One day, from the development machine's network; a deployment elsewhere sees different network latency.
The latency of a whole search: dedup and ranking (phases 7 and 8) must fit the remaining 1.0 s, and phase 10's live run measures the whole request.
Anchor recall counts 20 famous papers and is blind to precision; a smaller page may drop useful papers that are not anchors.

A3.question: What do the two shipped sources return today for the 20 P1 queries, so phase 8 judges the candidates production would actually rank?
A3.why: OpenAlex's ranking changed between the spike and A2 (D126): the frozen pools record a ranking OpenAlex no longer serves, and A2's 25-result pages are from 2026-10-04 and have no arXiv half. D126 requires a re-recording with the shipped request before phase 8 judges anything (D149, D150).
A3.queries: The 20 P1 queries: 10 topics x keyword and natural_language. Each is sent once to OpenAlex and once to arXiv, every request, URL and headers, built by the production adapter: scholiast.infrastructure.discovery.openalex.OpenAlexSource.request(text, limit=25) (D125's shipped page size) and scholiast.infrastructure.discovery.arxiv.ArxivSource().request(text, limit=50) (D120's AND construction, the shipped page size). 40 requests.
A3.order: Seeded with stream '<seed>/A3': the 20 queries are shuffled, and within each query the order of the two sources is shuffled. A query's two requests run one after the other, each waiting for its own host's pacing gap.
A3.connection: A new HTTP client, and so a new connection, for every request, as the production adapters open one per search. Bodies are decoded as the client receives them, as in P1.
A3.pacing: pacing['api.openalex.org'] and pacing['export.arxiv.org'], as P1: OpenAlex 1 s from the previous request start, arXiv 3 s from the previous response end and one connection. Retry-After and the host-stop rule apply as in pacing.
A3.timeouts: timeouts_s.api_connect and api_total, as P1: the tail is observed, not cut at D122's 2.0 s.
A3.no_repeats: As rules: a failure is an outcome, and no A3 request is repeated. A query whose request to one source failed is judged on the source that answered.
A3.measure: Reported, not decision inputs: per source, latency from request issued to last body byte (nearest-rank p50 and p95, a failed request counted as slower than any success) and the share answered within 2.0 s; per query, the overlap in OpenAlex work ids between A3's 25-result page and A2's 25-result page for the same query (drift since 2026-10-04); cost from x-ratelimit-cost-usd.
A3.decision_rule: None. A3 records the judging pools; it chooses nothing.
A3.outputs: Responses to data/eval/discovery-pools-a3.json.gz with a manifest (OpenAlex and arXiv metadata, CC0); numbers under addendum_a3 in spike/results/19_discovery_analysis.json. The spike's committed pools, A1's and A2's are not changed.
does_not_establish: One day's ranking from each source: OpenAlex changed its ranking once without notice (D126), and phase 10's live run sees its own day.
Anything about retrieval quality: phase 8 judges and reorders what the sources returned, so a relevant paper neither source returned is invisible to it.
The latency of a whole search: phase 10's live run measures the whole request.

A4.question: Does the shipped discovery search meet NFR-P1 live, by D158's rule; is the first search after a fresh start any different from the rest; does killing a source live still return partial results with each source's status (M4 criterion 5); and where are the 20 anchors today (D126)?
A4.why: M4 criterion 1 needs the whole pipeline measured against the live sources (fan-out, dedup, dense ranking and HTTP together), which no earlier pass did: A2 and A3 timed the sources alone, and phase 8b timed ranking on recorded bodies. D155's walkthrough saw OpenAlex miss the deadline on the first search after each of two starts and could not separate a fresh process from OpenAlex's own tail (D156). D126 asks for the anchors on the live run's own day.
A4.app: The real app on this machine: scholiast.api.app.create_app with its own lifespan, so D156's warm-up runs as shipped; no in-process worker, because nothing is ingested. Served by uvicorn on 127.0.0.1 with every production default for discovery: the 2.0 s deadline, OpenAlex 25 results, arXiv 50, arXiv's 3 s pacing, 10 searches a minute, the discovery cache. OpenAlex keyed from spike/.env, the key never written anywhere. Throwaway state: a testcontainers Postgres migrated to head, a fresh Qdrant collection per start, Redis database 11 on both Redis servers, emptied before the run and after it. One account, registered on the first start. The client is a separate process on the same machine.
A4.queries: 30: the 10 topics x keyword, natural_language and reversed_keyword. Each is searched once cold (not in the discovery cache), then once more, identically, as its cached repeat.
A4.order: Seeded with stream '<seed>/A4': the 30 queries are shuffled and dealt in order into 5 blocks of 6, one block per fresh start of the app. Within a start, each query's cold search is followed by its repeat.
A4.starts: 5. A start is a new app process; the client waits for /health/live, then logs in. The first cold search after each start is a 'first after start' sample, 5 of the 30.
A4.spacing: Each search begins at least 6.5 s after the previous one began, so neither the 10-a-minute rate limit nor arXiv's 3 s pacing (D123) refuses one. A search refused by either is an outcome and counts against its source.
A4.measured: Client side, per search: time from request sent to last response byte, HTTP status, partial, each source's status, the relevance signal, and each result's title, year, arXiv id and member sources with their ranks. Server side, recorded by wrapping httpx in the app process without changing what it sends: every outbound request's host, path (never the query string, which carries the key), status, and times to headers and to last byte; per search, when the fan-out ended and how long ranking took; and outbound requests made while each start boots.
A4.kill: M4 criterion 5, live, after the 30 searches. Three starts per source, each with that source's base URL pointed somewhere local: a port nobody listens on (refused; on this machine Windows takes 2.04 s to report it, so it is expected to read as a timeout at the 2.0 s deadline), a socket that accepts and never answers (hang), and a server that answers 500 at once (error; not 503, which the arXiv adapter reads as throttling and reports as rate_limited, because arXiv throttles with it). One cold search on each, the discovery cache emptied first, using the keyword queries of t01 to t06 in that order (OpenAlex refused, hang, error; then arXiv refused, hang, error). Checked and reported, not a decision input: HTTP 200, partial true, the killed source not ok, the other ok. Then one start with OpenAlex refused, held open for the UI check in the built-in browser: at most 3 searches, by hand.

budget.counting: 30 cold searches ask each source once; the 6 kill searches ask the surviving source once each, 3 per source; the UI check asks arXiv at most 3 times. Repeats of complete searches ask nothing. A repeat of a partial search asks the failed source again (D127), and that counts too. A killed source's own attempt goes to a local address and never reaches the source, but the wrapper counts it against that source's budget anyway, which only lowers the ceiling.
budget.enforcement: The httpx wrapper in the app process refuses any request to either host beyond its max, which the app then reports as that source's error.

A4.no_repeats: As rules: no search is repeated; a failed or partial search is an outcome. If the harness stops part-way, that is reported and the owner decides whether the rest runs.
A4.decision_rule: D158. Criterion 1 is met if and only if all four hold: (1) cold p95 <= 3.0 s over the 30 cold searches, nearest rank, a search that did not return 200 counted as slower than any that did; (2) cached p95 <= 0.4 s over the repeats of cold searches on which every source was ok; (3) each source ok on at least 24 of the 30 cold searches; (4) zero outbound requests during every repeat counted in (2). Otherwise criterion 1 is 'not met as written', with each failed condition and its cause. Repeats of partial cold searches are reported separately: failures are not cached (D127), so they ask the failed source again.
A4.reported: Not decision inputs: p50 and the maximum beside each p95; the split between fan-out, ranking and the rest; per source, time to headers and to last byte, and completion with a Wilson interval; the 5 first-after-start searches beside the other 25; startup time and its outbound requests (D157 expects none to huggingface.co); per anchor, its rank in its topic's keyword results today and which sources returned it, beside whether A3's recorded pages contained it.
A4.outputs: spike/results/20_discovery_live.json (tracked): every search's summary and every outbound request's record, no response bodies, no key, plus the computed numbers and the verdict; quoted in the M4 milestone log. Script: spike/scripts/20_discovery_live.py.
does_not_establish: Latency under concurrent load: one user, one search at a time.
Another day or another network: one machine, one connection, one day of each source's latency. OpenAlex has changed its ranking without notice before (D126).
A tight p95: at 30 searches it is the 29th value, close to the maximum; the 5 first-after-start searches are descriptive only.
Cold for the sources: these queries were sent to both before (P1, A2, A3), and what a source caches for itself is outside our control. Cold here means not in our cache.
Ranking quality: the anchors are 20 famous papers (D126); phase 8's judged set is the instrument for that.

A5.question: Does reusing one connection per source (pooled) let OpenAlex answer inside D122's 2.0 s deadline more often than a new connection per request (fresh, as shipped, D119); and where does a fresh request's time go?
A5.why: D160 (A4) measured OpenAlex inside 2.0 s on 15 of 29 cold searches, with headers at p50 0.99 s and then a near-constant 0.80 s of body on a fresh connection, which is consistent with TCP slow start over a long round trip. A4 recorded no connection-level timings, so that is a hypothesis. D161 plans this test; if pooling is adopted, A6 re-judges M4 criterion 1 end to end.
A5.arms: fresh: a new httpx.AsyncClient per request, exactly as the production adapters build it (follow_redirects=False, verify=the shared TLS context, the adapter's timeout), closed after the request. pooled: one httpx.AsyncClient per source for the whole condition, built the same way plus httpx.Limits(keepalive_expiry=120.0), so an idle connection is kept past the longer gap unless the server closes it. HTTP/1.1 in both, as shipped.
A5.requests: Every request is built by the production adapter: OpenAlexSource(key).request(text, limit=25) and ArxivSource().request(text, limit=50), the shipped page sizes. Nothing in the request is changed by either arm; the only addition is httpx's trace extension on the request object, which records timings and sends nothing.
A5.deadline: Both arms cut each request at 2.0 s from send to last body byte, as the production fan-out does (D122). A cut pooled request closes its connection, as it would in production, so the next pooled request pays a new one.
A5.queries: The 30 protocol queries: 10 topics x keyword, natural_language and reversed_keyword.
A5.conditions: short then long, each with new pooled clients. Within a condition each source is a lane, and the two lanes run at the same time, as the fan-out asks both at once. A lane works in periods of G seconds, each split into three equal slots: the pooled request for query i goes in the middle slot of period i, and the fresh request for query i in the first slot when i is even and in the last when i is odd, so the pooled gap stays G while which arm sends a query first alternates. G is 7 s for OpenAlex and 15 s for arXiv in the short condition, and 90 s for both in the long one. arXiv cannot run at 7 s: its pacing (one connection, 3 s from the previous response end) needs at least 5 s per slot when a request may take the full 2.0 s, so its short gap is the smallest that fits. A request whose pacing is not yet satisfied at its slot waits for it, and the actual gap is recorded. A lane that falls more than one slot behind its schedule (after a stall or a standby) shifts the rest of its schedule forward by its lateness, so later gaps return to G; each shift is recorded.
A5.order: Seeded with stream '<seed>/A5': the 30 queries are shuffled once, and that order is used by both lanes and both conditions.
A5.pacing: pacing['api.openalex.org'] and pacing['export.arxiv.org'] as in P1, across both arms on a host: OpenAlex 1 s from the previous request start; arXiv 3 s from the previous response end, one connection at a time.
A5.measured: Per request: arm, condition, lane, query, whether this arm sent the query first, the actual gap since the previous pooled request on the lane, status, outcome (ok, cut at the deadline, error, refused), bytes, and from the trace: connect (DNS and TCP), TLS handshake, time from send to response headers, body time, and whether the request reused a connection (no connect event). Never the URL's query string or any header.
A5.ok: A request is ok if it returned HTTP 200, its body was read completely within 2.0 s of send, and the production parser (parse_works, parse_feed) accepts it.
A5.standby: Pre-registered after A4 (D160): a request during which the machine entered modern standby (System log, Kernel-Power 506 between its start and end, checked after the run) is void, excluded from every number, and not repeated. Every record is written to disk as it completes. A pooled request whose actual gap since the lane's previous pooled request is outside 0.5 G to 1.5 G (as the first one after a standby is) is off-condition: it and the fresh request for the same query are excluded from every number and counted. The first pooled request of each condition has no gap and counts.

budget.counting: 30 queries x 2 arms x 2 conditions per source. Enforced in the harness; a request beyond the max is not sent.

A5.no_repeats: As rules: no request is repeated; a failure is an outcome. If the harness stops part-way, that is reported and the owner decides whether the rest runs.
A5.statistics: Completion per arm with Wilson intervals. The paired difference in completion (pooled minus fresh, per query, over the queries where neither request is void) with a 95% percentile interval from 10,000 paired bootstrap resamples of queries, seeded with stream '<seed>/A5/bootstrap'.
A5.decision_rule: Adopt pooling if and only if all three hold: (1) in the short condition, OpenAlex's paired completion difference is at least +0.15 and its interval excludes zero; (2) in the short condition, arXiv's pooled completion is not lower than fresh by more than 2 of 30 queries; (3) across the whole run, at most 1 pooled request that reused a connection fails with a connection error (a server-closed connection surfacing as an error). Otherwise pooling is not adopted. Adoption is a decision to build it; whether M4 criterion 1 is then met is A6's to say.
A5.reported: Not decision inputs: the long condition's results by the same measures; the reuse rate by condition and source; connect, TLS, header and body times on new against reused connections (slow start predicts a much faster body on a reused connection; server time predicts none); the order effect (first against second sender of a query); and cost from x-ratelimit-cost-usd.
A5.outputs: spike/results/21_pooling.json (tracked): every request's record, no bodies, no key, no query strings, plus the computed numbers and the verdict. Script: spike/scripts/21_pooling.py.
does_not_establish: NFR-P1 for the whole app: A5 times the sources alone; A6 runs the app.
Anything about the first search after a start: a pooled client's first request is a new connection in either arm.
A startup pre-connect, which would need a request to each source at every boot.
A user's occasional search beyond 90 s, or concurrent users.
Another day or network: one machine, one connection, one session; OpenAlex's speed varied from A3 to A4 by a day.

A6-multiday.question: On three different days, which of four configurations (OpenAlex at 25 or 15 results x a source deadline of 2.0 or 2.5 s, arXiv at 50) lets both sources finish inside the deadline on at least 80% of searches every day?
A6-multiday.why: M4 criterion 1's cold half is not met (D160): OpenAlex was inside 2.0 s on 15 of 29 cold searches in A4, and arXiv on 22 of 29. A5 showed the time is the sources' own, not our connections' (D163), and OpenAlex was inside 2.0 s on 29 of 30 the next day, so one day decides nothing (D164).
A6-multiday.days: Three runs, day 1 to day 3 in that order, on three different calendar days (local time), each starting at least 18 hours after the previous day's start; the start time is recorded. The harness refuses a day out of order or too soon.
A6-multiday.requests: Each day, every one of the 30 protocol queries (10 topics x keyword, natural_language, reversed_keyword) is sent to OpenAlex at 25 and at 15 results and to arXiv at 50, each request built by the production adapter: OpenAlexSource(key).request(text, limit=k) and ArxivSource().request(text, limit=50). Each is sent on a new client built as the production adapters build theirs (D119), so on a new connection, as shipped.
A6-multiday.timing: Timed to the last body byte, not cut: timeouts_s.api_connect and api_total, as P1, so the tail is observed and one measurement answers both deadlines. httpx's trace extension records the time to response headers. A request is ok if it returned HTTP 200 and the production parser (parse_works, parse_feed) accepts its body; it finished inside deadline D if it is ok and its last byte came within D of its send.
A6-multiday.order: Seeded per day with stream '<seed>/A6-multiday/day<N>': the 30 queries are shuffled. OpenAlex runs two passes over that order, 6 s apart from request start to request start: in pass 1 a query in an even position is sent at 25 and one in an odd position at 15, and in pass 2 the other way round, so each size is sent first for half the queries and a query's two requests are minutes apart. arXiv runs one pass over the same order at the same time, each request starting 12 s after the previous one started and at least 3 s after its response ended.
A6-multiday.pacing: pacing['api.openalex.org'] and pacing['export.arxiv.org'], as P1, are met by the order's spacing; a request whose pacing is not yet met waits for it.
A6-multiday.standby: As A5: a request during which the machine entered modern standby (Kernel-Power 506 between its send and its end) is void, excluded from every number, and not repeated. Every record is written to disk as it completes.

budget.counting: Per day 60 OpenAlex searches (30 queries x 2 page sizes) and 30 arXiv queries, for three days. Enforced in the harness across days; a request beyond the max is not sent.

A6-multiday.no_repeats: As rules: no request is repeated, and a failure is an outcome. If a day stops part-way, that is reported and the owner decides what follows.
A6-multiday.decision_rule: For each configuration and each day: OpenAlex at the configuration's page size and arXiv at 50 each finished inside the configuration's deadline on at least ceil(0.8 n) of their n valid requests that day (D158's 80%). A configuration passes if that holds for both sources on all three days. A6-multiday chooses the first passing configuration in the order listed under configurations. If 'as shipped' is chosen, nothing changes and A7 still has to re-judge criterion 1 end to end. If another is chosen, it is built and A7, an end-to-end live run with A4's design and D158's rule, re-judges criterion 1. If none passes, NFR-P1's cold half cannot be met with these two sources inside 3.0 s, and what follows is the owner's.
A6-multiday.reported: Not decision inputs: per day, source and page size, completion with Wilson intervals at deadlines 1.5, 2.0, 2.5 and 3.0 s, and time to headers and to last byte (nearest-rank p50 and p95); OpenAlex's pass effect (first against second request for a query); time of day; cost from x-ratelimit-cost-usd. The relevance cost of OpenAlex at 15, measured offline before A6-multiday (spike/results/22_truncation_relevance.json, D164): nDCG@10 -0.0002 [-0.012, +0.012] and 111 of 1,142 relevant papers no longer returned.
A6-multiday.outputs: spike/results/23_multiday.json (tracked), rewritten after each day: every request's record (no bodies, no key, no query strings), the per-day numbers, and after day 3 the verdict. Script: spike/scripts/23_multiday.py.
does_not_establish: NFR-P1 for the whole app: A6-multiday times the sources alone; A7 runs the app.
Three days are three samples of the sources' variability, not its distribution; a configuration that passes all three can still fail on a fourth.
One machine and one network; the time of day is recorded but not controlled.
Relevance at 15 beyond the offline estimate on A3's pools and D149's judgments.

outputs.what: scripts: search and lookups; PDF probe and downloads; analysis and log checker
request log: every API request with timings, status, selected headers and byte counts; no bodies, no keys; S2 identifiers hashed
analysis: every number the findings quote
frozen candidate pools: raw OpenAlex and arXiv response bodies for every session-1 and session-2 query, plus a manifest (dates, endpoints, parameters, protocol_sha256, counts, SHA-256 of the archive)
raw S2 response bodies and S2 identifiers
findings, with 'what this does not establish' above the numbers

pools_caveat: The pools reflect this protocol's query construction. If phase 2 changes it or the page size, the pools are re-recorded through the real adapters before any judging. Judgments attach to papers, not positions, so any already made carry over.
acceptance: The owner approved this protocol before the first live call, and every results file records its protocol_sha256.
P0's offline checks passed, including the checker mutant being caught.
The log checker, not a reading by eye, confirms: every source within budget; every pacing gap respected; zero requests to non-global addresses; zero redirects followed automatically.
Every planned request has a logged outcome: a response, a classified failure, or 'not sent' with its reason.
An ASM-1 verdict per source against the pass bars, with n beside every number and Wilson intervals on proportions.
An ASM-2 verdict with the full funnel under A1, A2 and A3.
The allowlist, dedup, licence, stability and phrasing evidence exists.
The pools reload with their SHA-256 verified, and git ls-files, git check-ignore -v and a grep show no S2 content, no PDF and no key in any tracked file.
All five gates green on the tree, with gate 4 printing 'Contracts: 3 kept, 0 broken'.
The findings put 'what this does not establish' above the numbers, and list the decisions they feed without taking them.
does_not_establish: Latency is from one home connection, one machine and two time windows: not a production number, and not reproducible.
At n=20, p95 is the second-worst value.
Relevance is a known-item check on 20 well-known papers chosen in advance, biased toward highly cited work. It is not a precision measurement; phase 8's judged set is.
Fetching a PDF's first bytes is not the same as the PDF being ingestible, and the preflight sample is at most 30.
Licence fields are often missing, and the spike cannot settle what arXiv's terms permit; it only counts.
Keyless S2 behaviour depends on everyone else's traffic at that moment.
Sources change: the pools are a snapshot as of their recording date.
The topics are ML/NLP only (T6).
